# Zami

Zami is [Zam](https://github.com/az4521/Zam), the Matrix client, ported to Expo and
React Native.

It isn't a GitHub fork. It's Zam's full history, merged from an `upstream` remote, plus
files Zami adds. Every upstream file (code, tests, styles, docs and assets) has a Zami
version next to it, and Zami develops there; the Expo app only loads those. What the
Expo app doesn't use gets none: configuration for SvelteKit, Vite and npm, and the other
platforms Expo replaces (Capacitor, Electron, Flatpak).

```
src/lib/stores/toasts.svelte.ts                    upstream
src/lib/stores/toasts.svelte.zami.ts               Zami: a copy, kept in sync by three-way merges
src/lib/components/layout/Splash.svelte            upstream
src/lib/components/layout/Splash.svelte.zami.tsx   Zami: the React Native translation
static/favicon.png, static/favicon.zami.png        upstream, and Zami's copy
apps/zami/                                         Zami: the Expo app
packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/                     Zami: its own code (Flatcap packages)
```

**Zami never edits Zam's files, with one exception:** the root `package.json` is Zami's
workspace manifest, so the repository root is a Flatcap workspace (Bun, Vite+). Bun reads
no other manifest name, so this one file is overridden; Zam's version keeps syncing as
`package.zami.json`, and `.gitattributes` keeps Zami's on every upstream merge. Vite+
needs no override: it reads `vite.config.js` before `vite.config.ts`, so Zami's
`vite.config.js` takes precedence over Zam's untouched `vite.config.ts`. Merging upstream
never conflicts, and a scheduled workflow does the rest:

1. It merges upstream.
2. It merges upstream's changes into the copied Zami files.
3. Claude (Opus 5.5) migrates upstream's changes to the translated components and
   resolves conflicts, checking its work against upstream's own tests.
4. It opens a pull request for review.

## Setup and running

```sh
git remote add upstream https://github.com/az4521/Zam.git   # once per clone
git fetch upstream
vp install
vpx _dev              # iOS simulator: build if needed, install, launch, serve JS
vpx _dev android      # Android emulator or device
vpx _dev start        # only the dev server, for an app that's already installed
```

Zam's build-time settings (`VITE_*`) are Expo environment variables here, named
`EXPO_PUBLIC_*` (`import.meta.env.VITE_FOO` reads `EXPO_PUBLIC_FOO`) and inlined when the
dev server bundles the app, so set them before `vpx _dev`:

- `EXPO_PUBLIC_PUSH_GATEWAY_URL`: the notify endpoint of the Sygnal push gateway that
  delivers Zami's iOS pushes (`https://…/_matrix/push/v1/notify`). That Sygnal needs an
  `apns` app with the id `com.leonsilicon.zami` (the bundle id) and Zami's APNs key, with
  `platform: sandbox` for development builds. Unset, the iOS app registers no pusher (Zam's
  own gateway, its default, has no app for Zami) and shows notifications only while it's
  running.

## Editors

Zam's own files are hidden in the editor, so the file tree shows Zami's versions
(`*.zami.*`) and Zami's code:

- **VS Code:** open `zami.code-workspace` (VS Code offers to when you open the folder).
  An upstream file is hidden only while its Zami version exists beside it, so components
  not ported yet stay visible. To see everything, open the folder without the workspace.
- **Zed:** `.zed/settings.json` applies automatically.

Both files are generated by `vpx _zami editor`, which `_zami sync` and `_zami done` rerun;
`_zami check` fails if they're out of date. Neither overrides Zam's `.vscode/settings.json`.

## Layout

Any code Zami writes that isn't the Zami version of a Zam file goes in a Flatcap package
under `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/`. A package's `_name.ts` scripts run as
`vpx _name` from anywhere in the repository.

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/zami` | The Expo app (`@-apps/zami`) |
| `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/ports` | `_zami`: maps upstream files to Zami versions, syncs and checks them |
| `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/metro` | Metro config: resolves only `.zami.` files in Zam's tree; compiles rune modules; handles Vite's build-time features |
| `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/vite` | The same for Vite, so upstream's tests run against the Zami files |
| `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/sveltekit` | Stand-ins for `$app/environment`, `$app/navigation` and `$app/state`, and for the tsconfig `svelte-kit sync` generates |
| `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/svelte-react` | `useRune`/`useDeepRune`: React components re-render when Svelte runes change |
| `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/icons` | `lucide-svelte` for the app: lucide-react-native icons that take Zam's Tailwind classes |
| `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/rn` | What translations share in place of web features: `Portal`, `Html`, `Image`/`mediaSource` |
| `packages/com/leonsilicon/zami/dev` | `_dev`: builds, installs and runs the app with its dev server |
| `zami-ports.json` | Which upstream files have a Zami version (all but the unused configuration in `exclude`), and the override (`package.json`) |
| `zami-ports.lock.json` | The upstream commit each Zami file was last synced with (written by `_zami`) |
| `zami.code-workspace`, `.zed/settings.json` | Editor settings that hide Zam's files (generated by `_zami editor`) |
| `patches/` | Uniwind patch: Zam's `[data-theme]` themes and `rgb(var(--x-rgb) / a)` colors |
| [`.github/PORTING.md`](./PORTING.md) | How to write and update Zami files |
| [`.github/workflows/zami-upstream-sync.yml`](./workflows/zami-upstream-sync.yml) | The sync bot |

## Checks

```sh
vp check              # format, lint and types: Zami's own code and the Zami files
vp fmt                # format them (`vp lint` lints them)
vp run typecheck
vp run test           # Zami's tooling tests, then upstream Zam's tests against the Zami files
vp run test:zam       # only upstream's tests
vp run bundle         # bundle the app's JS for iOS and Android with Metro
vpx _zami check       # the porting invariants
vpx _zami status      # how many files are ported, stale or missing
```

Vite+ covers Zami's own code (`apps/`, `packages/`) and the `.zami.` files in Zam's tree,
never Zam's own files. The root `vite.config.js` ignores everything in Zam's tree except
the Zami files, and among those it skips whatever Zam's `.prettierignore` skips (such as
the vendored code in `static/`).

- **Formatting:** Zami files use Zam's own Prettier options (4-space indent, 80 columns),
  so most copies stay byte-identical to upstream. Oxfmt formats a few constructs
  differently from Prettier, so a few dozen copies differ from upstream only in
  formatting. `package.zami.json` isn't formatted: Prettier formats `package.json` the way
  `JSON.stringify` does, which oxfmt can't.
- **Linting:** copies skip Flatcap's rules and the ones Zam's code doesn't follow;
  translations add React's. Type-aware rules read Zam's `tsconfig.json`, which extends
  `.svelte-kit/tsconfig.json`. Zami's postinstall writes that file, in place of
  `svelte-kit sync`, from `@-/com.leonsilicon.zami.sveltekit`'s
  `tsconfig.svelte-kit.json`. It gives type information without type-checking Zam's code
  (`noCheck`). `vp run typecheck` type-checks the Zami files the app imports.

At the root, use `vp run test` rather than a bare `vp test`, which would pick up Zam's
`vitest.config.ts`.

## Upstream's tests

Every upstream test has an Zami copy (`foo.test.zami.ts`), and `vp run test:zam` runs them
against Zami's files: every import, and every `require` of a file in Zam's tree, loads
the `.zami.` version (`@-/com.leonsilicon.zami.vite`), in jsdom as Zam does. So when Zami
changes a copy, or the sync bot migrates one, upstream's own tests check it.

- The 18 tests that render Svelte components are left out until they're rewritten for
  React Native (`componentTestFiles` lists them).
- Two copies are changed to inspect the Zami files rather than upstream's
  (`i18n.test.zami.ts`, `heavyDepImports.test.zami.ts`), because they scan the source
  tree, which now holds both.
